title: Correct attribution for retried/deduped tokens after quota reconciliation across regions
creator: Aisha Khan
description:
Symptom: Several tenants report that the per-model breakdowns in Console show negative deltas or sudden drops the day after large quota reconciliations. These anomalies correlate with multi-region replay jobs and a recent change to the rate-limit reconciliation logic that dedupes retry fan-in without attaching provenance metadata.

Hypothesis: When rate-limit retries are reconciled across regions, the ledger deduplication step removes retry events but the streaming prefix-aggregation layer has already emitted tokens into the realtime projection. Later the backfill/replay deduplicates the ledger without an explicit provenance flag, causing the reconstructed per-model counts to be lower than the realtime-sourced charts. Additionally, the dedupe window uses non-deterministic shard timestamps which causes different regions to choose different winners for ambiguous requests, leading to model attribution splits (e.g., alias -> canonical model mapping flips).

Impact: Affects Console per-model heatmaps and top-model lists for ~3% of enterprise tenants during heavy cross-region failover/retry events. Impacts billing reconciliations for a small subset of Reserved capacity customers who reconcile within 24-72 hours of the event. Customer complaints include incorrect cost allocation, unexplained spikes followed by negative corrections, and temporary quota exhaustion indications.

Success criteria:
- No negative deltas occur in reconstructed daily aggregates after reconciliation runs (benchmarked with synthetic replay). 
- Per-model attribution remains stable (<=0.1% variance) across regions for the synthetic multi-region replay set.
- Console and billing reports show matching token totals within rounding tolerance after reconciliation.

Plan:
1) Instrumentation: add a reconciliation_provenance tag to ledger events produced by rate-limit reconciler and backfill jobs. Emit reconciliation_id and origin_region as metadata to all reconstructed events.
2) Deterministic dedupe: change dedupe selection to use (request_id, reconciliation_id) deterministic tie-breaker instead of shard timestamp; document migration plan for historical reconciled batches.
3) Projection change: make realtime projection honor reconciliation_provenance flags and avoid double-subtracting already-emitted tokens by checking event provenance before applying edits.
4) Backfill dry-run: run synthetic multi-region replay for 3 largest impacted tenants in staging, compare Console aggregates against golden-export.
5) Rollout: feature-flagged deploy to a small set of tenants, monitor net token delta and per-model variance for 48h; if green, ramp.
6) Dashboard: add a reconciliation health panel in Console showing reconciliation_id lag, replays in-progress, and per-tenant delta histogram.

Risks and trade-offs:
- Adding provenance metadata increases event size and storage by ~1.2% — acceptable for correctness guarantees.
- Changing dedupe semantics could alter historical reconciled ledgers; we'll avoid rewriting past reconciled batches and instead mark them as legacy (handled by reconciliation_id null checks).
- Additional projection checks may add CPU overhead to realtime writers; we will benchmark and add autoscale knobs if needed.

Telemetry and observability:
- New metrics: reconciliation_id_count, reconciliation_latency_seconds, provenance_mismatch_events_total, per_model_variance_after_replay_percent.
- Grafana alerts: per-tenant negative-delta rate > 0.1% for 1h, reconciliation lag > 6h.

Rollout and rollback:
- Deploy behind feature flag mapped to customer tags. If negative-delta increases or reconciliation_latency spikes > 2x baseline, roll back flag and investigate.

Artifacts and links:
- Confluence runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Retry+Dedupe+Reconciliation+Design
- Staging dashboard (golden replay): https://grafana.internal.redwood/console/goldens/replay-multi-region
- Design PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/designs/pull/492
- WIP implementation PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/2417

Notes: This ticket focuses on correctness and provenance. Follow-up tickets will address archival compaction and long-term ledger storage optimizations.
